title_en: Ren Jianguo v. Reeducation through Labor Committee — dispute over review decision on reeducation through labor
keywords_en: administrative; administrative case of re-education through labor; first instance; second instance; basic people's court; intermediate people's court; Shanxi Province; natural person; state organ; Administrative Procedure Law; Trial Measures for Re-education through Labor; applicable subjects of re-education through labor; reference application of local regulations; error in application of law; revocation of original decision; obstruction of official duties; decision on re-education through labor; administrative litigation; administration according to law
full_text_en:
Ren Jianguo v. Luliang Administrative Office Reeducation through Labor Management Committee — dispute over reeducation through labor review decision

Plaintiff: Ren Jianguo, male, 29 years old, driver of Gaoyang Coal Mine, Xiaoyi City, Shanxi Province.

Defendant: Luliang Administrative Office Reeducation through Labor Management Committee, Shanxi Province.

Legal Representative: Hua Derong, Director.

The plaintiff, Ren Jianguo, dissatisfied with the review decision of the Luliang Administrative Office Reeducation through Labor Management Committee of Shanxi Province, which upheld the original decision to subject him to reeducation through labor for one year, filed an administrative lawsuit with the Lishi County People's Court of Shanxi Province.

Plaintiff's Allegations: After a dispute arose between the plaintiff and the mine director, Zhang Fubao, the defendant gave biased credence to one side, exaggerated the facts, and made a decision to subject the plaintiff to reeducation through labor for one year. The plaintiff does not fall within the category of persons subject to reeducation through labor, and the defendant's decision lacks any legal basis. To create an impression of handling the case in accordance with the law, the defendant merely stated in its decision that it was "pursuant to the relevant provisions of the State Council on reeducation through labor," without citing any specific articles of those provisions. After the plaintiff lawfully applied for review, the defendant was unable to directly address the issues raised by the plaintiff, merely evading the matter with the empty phrase that "the original decision had clear facts, accurate characterization, and appropriate punishment," and then ex officio issued a review decision upholding the original decision. The plaintiff requests that the People's Court revoke this specific administrative act of the defendant.

Defendant's Defense: The facts that the plaintiff, Ren Jianguo, used violence to obstruct the mine director, Zhang Fubao, from performing his duties are clear. Pursuant to Article 8, Item (2) of the "Provisions of the People's Government of Shanxi Province on Protecting the Lawful Performance of Duties by Enterprise Directors and Managers": "Those who obstruct directors or managers from lawfully performing their duties by means of violence or threat, where the act is not yet sufficient for criminal punishment, may be subjected to reeducation through labor." The defendant decided to subject the plaintiff to reeducation through labor and completed the reeducation through labor procedures in accordance with the relevant procedural regulations of the State Council on reeducation through labor. Therefore, the defendant's specific administrative act correctly applied the law, its procedures were lawful, and it should be upheld.

Facts Found by the Lishi County People's Court: On the afternoon of July 15, 1992, the plaintiff, Ren Jianguo, went to the office of the Gaoyang Coal Mine director, Zhang Fubao, and saw Zhang Fubao talking with a mine cadre. Ren Jianguo asked the cadre to leave for a moment so that he could discuss the housing allocation matter with Zhang Fubao. Zhang Fubao told Ren Jianguo to go out first, saying they were discussing work. Ren Jianguo did not leave, so Zhang Fubao stepped forward and pushed Ren Jianguo outward. At that point, Ren Jianguo grabbed Zhang Fubao's collar and pushed and pulled him back and forth, and also grabbed his hair. After being劝阻 by others, the incident subsided. Based on the above facts, and on the grounds that Ren Jianguo refused to be dissuaded, used violence to push and pull the mine director, obstructed the director from performing his duties, and affected the normal production of the enterprise, the defendant, on August 28, 1992, decided to subject Ren Jianguo to reeducation through labor for one year, pursuant to the relevant provisions of the State Council on reeducation through labor and Article 8, Item (2) of the "Provisions of the People's Government of Shanxi Province on Protecting the Lawful Performance of Duties by Enterprise Directors and Managers." Ren Jianguo disagreed and, in accordance with the law, applied for review to the defendant on September 9. On September 28, the defendant upheld the original reeducation through labor decision on the grounds that the original decision had clear facts, accurate characterization, and appropriate punishment. Ren Jianguo remained dissatisfied with the review decision and thus filed this lawsuit.

Opinion of the Lishi County People's Court: Article 52, Paragraph 1 of the "Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China" provides: "When hearing administrative cases, the People's Courts shall take laws, administrative regulations, and local regulations as the basis." The administrative regulations that can serve as the basis for hearing administrative cases concerning reeducation through labor include: the "Decision on Questions Concerning Reeducation through Labor" promulgated by the State Council on August 3, 1957; the "Supplementary Provisions on Reeducation through Labor" promulgated by the State Council on November 29, 1979; and the "Trial Measures for Reeducation through Labor" forwarded by the State Council and issued by the Ministry of Public Security on January 21, 1982. These three regulations provide detailed provisions on the categories of persons subject to reeducation through labor, and the approval and management procedures, but none of them authorize local people's governments to formulate separate implementing measures. The categories of persons subject to reeducation through labor specified in these three regulations are very clear, and they do not contain any provision similar to Article 8, Item (2) of the "Provisions of the People's Government of Shanxi Province on Protecting the Lawful Performance of Duties by Enterprise Directors and Managers," which states: "Those who obstruct directors or managers from lawfully performing their duties by means of violence or threat, where the act is not yet sufficient for criminal punishment, may be subjected to reeducation through labor." Therefore, this provision in the Shanxi provincial government's regulatory document can only be understood as follows: only when a person who falls within the categories of persons subject to reeducation through labor under the regulations also commits an act of obstructing a director or manager from lawfully performing duties by means of violence or threat, and the act is not yet sufficient for criminal punishment, may that person be subjected to reeducation through labor. Otherwise, reeducation through labor cannot be imposed on that person solely based on this regulatory document.

The plaintiff, Ren Jianguo, refused to be dissuaded and used methods such as pushing, pulling, and grabbing hair against Zhang Fubao. This constitutes an illegal act infringing upon Zhang Fubao's personal rights. However, this type of illegal act does not fall within the scope regulated by China's reeducation through labor regulations, and subjecting him to reeducation through labor does not comply with the provisions of those regulations. When the defendant decided to subject Ren Jianguo to reeducation through labor, because it could not cite specific provisions on the categories of persons subject to reeducation through labor under the reeducation through labor regulations, it vaguely stated that its decision was based on the relevant provisions of the State Council on reeducation through labor and Article 8, Item (2) of the "Provisions of the People's Government of Shanxi Province on Protecting the Lawful Performance of Duties by Enterprise Directors and Managers." Furthermore, when Ren Jianguo filed an application for review, the defendant could not refute the issues with proper legal reasoning and evidence, and instead issued a review decision stating "clear facts, accurate characterization, appropriate punishment, original decision upheld." This not only constitutes an improper application of the law but also disregards the citizen's exercise of legitimate rights of appeal, which is erroneous. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 54, Item (2) of the "Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," the Lishi County People's Court rendered judgment on December 5, 1992: The review decision made by the defendant, the Luliang Administrative Office Reeducation through Labor Management Committee of Shanxi Province, upholding the original decision to subject the plaintiff, Ren Jianguo, to reeducation through labor for one year, and the original decision to subject Ren Jianguo to reeducation through labor for one year, are both revoked. Litigation costs of RMB 100 shall be borne by the defendant.

After the judgment of first instance was announced, the defendant, the Luliang Administrative Office Reeducation through Labor Management Committee of Shanxi Province, refused to accept it and appealed to the Luliang Intermediate People's Court of Shanxi Province, on the grounds that "when hearing administrative cases, the People's Courts shall refer to local regulations."

Opinion of the Luliang Intermediate People's Court of Shanxi Province: Article 53 of the Administrative Procedure Law provides: "When hearing administrative cases, the People's Courts shall refer to regulations formulated and issued by ministries and commissions under the State Council in accordance with laws and the administrative regulations, decisions, and orders of the State Council, as well as regulations formulated and issued by the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, the people's governments of cities where the people's governments of provinces and autonomous regions are located, and the people's governments of larger cities approved by the State Council, in accordance with laws and the administrative regulations of the State Council." The regulations referred to here as being subject to reference are those formulated in accordance with laws and administrative regulations of the State Council. Regulations that are not formulated in accordance with laws and administrative regulations, or whose content conflicts with laws and administrative regulations, are not within the scope of reference by the People's Courts. The administrative regulations of the State Council on reeducation through labor clearly specify the categories of persons subject to reeducation through labor. Article 8, Item (2) of the "Provisions of the People's Government of Shanxi Province on Protecting the Lawful Performance of Duties by Enterprise Directors and Managers" expands the scope of application of reeducation through labor. When referring to such regulations, the People's Courts shall only apply them within the scope consistent with the administrative regulations. That is, when a person who falls within the categories of persons subject to reeducation through labor under the administrative regulations commits an act of obstructing a director or manager from lawfully performing duties by means of violence or threat, that person may be subjected to reeducation through labor. If a person does not fall within the categories of persons subject to reeducation through labor, then reeducation through labor cannot be imposed on that person solely by referring to such regulations. Both the substantive and procedural provisions of laws and administrative regulations must be applied comprehensively and accurately in order to handle cases according to law. Applying only procedural provisions without applying substantive provisions, or applying only substantive provisions without applying procedural provisions, does not constitute handling cases according to law. The original trial court's judgment, which revoked the decision of the appellant, the Luliang Administrative Office Reeducation through Labor Management Committee of Shanxi Province, to subject the appellee, Ren Jianguo, to reeducation through labor for one year, on the grounds of erroneous application of law, is correct. The appellant's appeal argument that "when hearing administrative cases, the People's Courts shall refer to local regulations" is not accepted. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 61, Item (1) of the Administrative Procedure Law, the Luliang Intermediate People's Court of Shanxi Province rendered judgment on January 6, 1993: The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed. Litigation costs for the second instance of RMB 100 shall be borne by the appellant.
